title: Guest room
topic: A friend is measuring a bigger guest bed against the walkway
blurb: A friend is swapping the guest bed and checking the walkway.
prompt: A friend just sent this in the group chat. Tap a line if something doesn't add up, or let it pass.

segments.label: The swap
segments.text: Putting a 6-foot bed in the guest room to replace the 5-foot one that's in there now.

segments.label: The layout
segments.text: The current bed sits tucked under the window, leaving a 2-foot aisle in front of the closet doors.

segments.label: The math
segments.text: Going up a foot in width trims half a foot per side, leaving a 1.5-foot aisle — still clears the closet.

segments.label: The order
segments.text: I'll order it tonight before the weekend sale ends.

conclusion: A foot wider means half a foot off each side, so the closet walkway only shrinks to 1.5 feet.

flaws.original: One side is already against the wall, so the whole extra foot comes out of the walkway — that's 1 foot left, not 1.5.
flaws.corrupted: Going up a foot in width trims half a foot per side, leaving a 1.5-foot aisle — still clears the closet.

diagnosis_choices.label: One side is against the wall, so the walkway loses a full foot — 1 foot left, not 1.5.
A 6-foot bed plus a 2-foot walkway takes 8 feet, and the 7-foot room can't fit a 6-foot bed at all.
Closet doors need a full 2-foot clearance to swing open, so even a 1.5-foot walkway already blocks them.
Splitting 1 foot into two halves only trims 6 inches off the room total, leaving the walkway at 1.5.

fix_choices.label: Subtract the full extra foot from the walkway: 2 feet minus 1 leaves 1 foot.
Pull the 6-foot bed 6 inches off the window wall so both sides split the extra width evenly.
Keep the 5-foot bed because a 6-foot bed won't leave any usable walkway in a 7-foot room.
Push the bed flush against the closet instead so the 1.5-foot walkway sits along the window.

flaws.explanation: The bed can't grow through the wall. That whole extra foot comes straight out of your walkway.
flaws.why_tempting: Splitting a width change 'half and half' feels automatic. It's easy to skip that one edge is already tight against a wall.
flaws.catch_rule: If one side of a bed or desk is already against a wall, every extra inch of width comes out of the open side.
flaws.hint: The current bed is already tight against one wall. Where can the extra foot actually go?

practice.problem: A sofa sits along one wall with a 90cm gap to the coffee table. A new sofa is 20cm deeper. A friend says, '10cm off each side, still 80cm to the table.' What's wrong?
practice.answer: The back is already against the wall, so all 20cm come out of the gap. That's 70cm left, not 80.

diagnosis: Standard queen beds are 5 feet wide and kings are 6.5 feet, so a 6-foot bed leaves out the bed frame width.
Replacing a 5-foot bed with a 6-foot one adds 20% to the footprint, which doesn't match the 1-foot math later.
A 6-foot bed is also longer head-to-foot, so comparing width alone misses the wall by the door.
Swapping from 5 feet to 6 feet adds 12 inches, which shrinks the room by 2 feet when you count both sides.
fix: Measure the bed frame width (usually 6.3–6.5 feet) instead of the 6-foot mattress size.
Check the length from headboard to wall before comparing widths.
Account for the 20% width jump on both the window and closet walls.
Stick with a 5.5-foot bed frame so the extra width stays under a foot.

diagnosis: A 5-foot bed plus a 2-foot walkway makes the room 7 feet wide, which is too narrow for a closet door anyway.
Pushing the bed against the window wall blocks the curtain, so you already have a 6-inch gap there.
Measuring the walkway from the mattress edge ignores the 6-inch baseboard and frame overhang.
Leaving 2 feet on one side means 1 foot on each side if you center the bed, not 2 feet total.
fix: Measure wall-to-closet directly instead of adding 5 feet plus 2 feet.
Center the current 5-foot bed so there is a 1-foot walkway on both sides.
Subtract 6 inches for curtains and trim before sizing the walkway.
Check whether the closet has sliding doors before worrying about the 2-foot gap.

diagnosis: Ordering tonight before measuring the stairwell means a 6-foot mattress might not make the turn upstairs.
Weekend sales usually extend into Monday, so rushing tonight risks a restocking fee.
Ordering without checking the closet door swing means even 1.5 feet might jam the hinge.
Ordering a 6-foot bed tonight locks you into an 8-foot layout in a 7-foot room.
fix: Measure the closet door swing and stairwell width before placing the order.
Wait until tomorrow and tape a 6-foot rectangle on the guest room floor first.
Check the store's return fee in case the 1-foot walkway is too tight.
Order the 5-foot replacement tonight instead while the sale is still on.
